note: gap_hours is 3 against the 01:10Z weekly, but that weekly was a duplicate-week stand-down publishing zero entries; the last fire to publish operational entries was 2026-08-23T0409Z-intel, ~24 h before this run's nominal start. The 24 h floor therefore covers the real operational delta exactly.

watchdog.action: Phase 1 was allowed to complete (the sub-agents had only just started and are the run's entire research surface); no scope widening, no research respawn after S3's failure, single-pass composition, and the overrun is disclosed in the run record.

S1.verdict: genuinely quiet vulnerability window; every fresh signal traced to already-covered ground

S2.verdict: caught the BACS half-year report inside its embargo lift; Berlin Landesnetz re-checked and unchanged

S3.verdict: TERMINATED by a content-classifier trip ([cyber] safeguard) ~12 min in; research domain uncovered this run

S4.verdict: one qualifying item; window dominated by settled ground

candidates.gate: PD-11(c) and (d) plus PD-9. The home-region authority's own semi-annual assessment of the landscape this constituency defends, published inside this run's window. Deep-dive criterion 4 (newly published periodic report of high relevance); rotation check: no annual-report deep dive in the trailing 30 days, and deep_dives_today was 0.
candidates.deep_read: Main agent re-fetched the 23-page PDF in binary (the sub-agent's copy was corrupted: 2,840,294 B mangled vs 1,733,418 B clean) and extracted its full text after stubbing a broken cryptography/_cffi_backend binding that blocks every PDF library in this container. Entry composed from the report body, not the press release.

candidates.gate: PD-11(b) and (d). Still no vendor fix for a privilege-escalation chain against a baseline endpoint control, so detection is the entire available control — and the published mechanism supplies the detection package the prior entries could not.
candidates.caveat: The LevelBlue post names no CVE anywhere (re-confirmed by case-insensitive grep of the freshly fetched body). The link to CVE-2026-69414 is this pipeline's reading of two accounts of the same named technique, and the entry says so.

candidates.gate: Correction of a published error that overstates exposure. Red Hat's structured product-state table, re-parsed this run, carries 11 Fixed rows and 2 Not-affected rows; no product is affected-and-unfixed.

PD-11(d). Teams is universal across this constituency's estate and the delivery inverts the direction staff are trained to distrust. Independently corroborated this run: the BACS half-year report describes the same email-bombing-then-Teams-helpdesk-impersonation chain against Swiss targets, citing Unit 42.
PD-9. Newly published periodic report; the W34 weekly does not mention it at all.
PD-11(d) with a concrete hardening lever: none of the four largest measured leak surfaces is the current working tree, so a clean secret scan of HEAD does not answer the question.
PD-11(d). A dead-drop carrier the W34 C2 synthesis does not cover, and the source's own qualification makes it the cheapest hunt in the set rather than the hardest.

Breach gate criterion (c): ShinyHunters is an actor this store already tracks against European targets, and the same-actor read matters more than the victim. The transferable lesson is the control that capped the blast radius (device-trust binding) plus a detection sequence in identity-provider logs.
candidates.framing: The leak-site claim is the attacker's unverified assertion and is not the entry's basis; the victim's own writeup is.

candidates.gate: PD-11(d). Partially covered (named inside two W34 synthesis entries) but with no dedicated entry and five unregistered malware families; the reusable content is the DLL-sideloading pairing discriminator.
